title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/16/2026

Reason for Admission:
The patient is an 89-year-old female who presented to the emergency department with a fever and symptoms of a urinary tract infection.

Hospital Course:
During her stay, the patient was evaluated for urosepsis. She was started on intravenous fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics to manage her systemic symptoms and localized infection. She remained stable throughout her hospitalization, with clinical improvement noted over several days. She tolerated her medications well and maintained adequate hydration. She was transitioned to oral therapy prior to discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Urosepsis
2. Urinary tract infection

Discharge Medications:
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily
- Acetaminophen 650 mg as needed for fever

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with her primary care physician in one week for a reassessment of her urinary symptoms and to monitor her progress.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
05/16/2026
explanations: 'Urosepsis' is a nonspecific term with no default code and is not the same as sepsis: query the provider. No sepsis code.

distractors.why: Urosepsis is not sepsis; it needs a provider query.
